events.title: The Boston Massacre
events.description: On a snowy night in Boston, a crowd confronted British soldiers outside the Custom House. The soldiers fired into the crowd and killed five colonists, among them Crispus Attucks.
events.significance: Patriot leaders widely publicized the shooting. It deepened colonial anger at British rule and helped push the colonies toward the American Revolution.

events.title: Churchill Popularizes the 'Iron Curtain'
events.description: Winston Churchill gave a speech at Westminster College in Fulton, Missouri. He warned that an 'iron curtain' had descended across Europe, dividing the continent.
events.significance: The phrase became shorthand for the East-West divide. It captured the start of the Cold War and shaped how the West described Soviet influence.

events.title: Death of Joseph Stalin
events.description: Soviet leader Joseph Stalin died in Moscow on the evening of March 5, after a cerebral hemorrhage. He had ruled the USSR for almost three decades.
events.significance: His death set off a power struggle in the Kremlin. It led to Nikita Khrushchev's rise and to a gradual easing of the harshest Soviet repression.

events.title: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty Takes Effect
events.description: The Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons entered into force. China, France, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom and the United States were the nuclear powers that took part.
events.significance: It remains the cornerstone of global efforts to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons and to promote disarmament and peaceful nuclear cooperation.

events.title: Voyager 1 Reaches Jupiter
events.description: NASA's Voyager 1 made its closest approach to Jupiter, passing about 172,000 miles from the planet. It captured detailed images of the planet and its moons, including volcanic activity on Io.
events.significance: The flyby revealed the first active volcanoes seen beyond Earth. It transformed scientists' understanding of the outer solar system.
